blocks.content: The Chairman or any other member of a Public Service Commission shall only be removed from his office by order of the President on the ground of proved misbehaviour after the Supreme Court inquiry.

items: Crucial distinction: The Governor appoints State PSC members, but ONLY the President can remove them.
The Supreme Court's report and advice during the removal inquiry under Article 317 is strictly binding on the President.
Pending the Supreme Court inquiry, the Governor can suspend an SPSC member, whereas the President suspends a UPSC member.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Members of both Central and State Public Service Commissions can only be removed from office by the President of India.
Although the Governor appoints members of a State Public Service Commission, the Governor has no power to remove them.
Removal on grounds of proved misbehaviour requires a mandatory reference to and inquiry by the Supreme Court.
The advice tendered by the Supreme Court following an inquiry under Article 317 is binding on the President.
Other grounds for removal include insolvency, engaging in paid employment outside duties, or infirmity of mind or body.
